name: Charge pump · doubler and inverter, chip (LT1054)
description: One LT1054 doubling and inverting at once, as the Klon's IC3 does (Aion FX Refractor; Microchip TC1044S data sheet (DS21348A), Figure 9): about twice V+ less two diode drops on V18, and about -V+ on VNEG. Label the stages it powers V18 and VNEG (an op-amp's V+ and V- pins: 27 V across it). C3 and D1, D2 make the doubler, C4 the inverter (D-226); C1 and C2 are the reservoirs. The LT1054 gives up to 100 mA; a TC1044S (U1's settings) does for a few op-amps. The Klon uses 1N4001s for D1, D2; Schottkys (1N5817) drop less.

notes.part:U1: Doubler and inverter at once: pin 2 swings between ground and V+, lifting the D1/D2 junction through C3 and pulling pin 4 below ground through C4; pin 5 (VOUT) is the negative output. Supply: pin 8 is the chip's supply input, fed from the pedal's V+ (the DC jack or the battery, through the input filter). The pump draws its current in short pulses at its switching rate; a bulk electrolytic on V+ (10-100 µF, such as the Input filter block's 47 Ω and 100 µF) supplies them close by, so they don't travel back along V+ and whine in the other stages. A pedal that already has one on V+ needs no second cap here (one close to pin 8 helps a little on a long board). A pedal with none, such as a bare battery fuzz like the Rangemaster, needs one: the "Supply without a bulk capacitor" warning says so.
notes.part:C3: Doubler's pump cap: the bigger, the lower V18's output resistance.
notes.part:C4: Inverter's flying cap: the bigger, the lower VNEG's output resistance.
notes.part:D1: D1 charges C3 from V+; D2 passes its charge on to V18.
notes.part:C1: V18's reservoir: holds it up between the pump's pulses.
notes.part:C2: VNEG's reservoir: its + side goes to ground (VNEG is below it).
notes.net:V18: About 17.5 V from 9 V: 2 × V+ less two diode drops and the pump's output resistance.
notes.net:VNEG: About -9 V: -V+ less the pump's output resistance × the current drawn.
